# GISAID Data Cleaning

## Remove Name duplicates and sequences with illegal nucleotide characters
```{shell}
#| eval: false

# h1n1 
seqkit rmdup -n source/gisaid_h1n1_sequences.fasta > source/gisaid_h1n1_sequences.rmdup.fasta
seqkit grep -s -r -i -p "^[ATCGatcg]+$" source/gisaid_h1n1_sequences.rmdup.fasta > source/gisaid_h1n1_sequences.rmdupn.noambig.fasta

# h3n2
seqkit rmdup -n source/gisaid_h3n2_sequences.fasta > source/gisaid_h3n2_sequences.rmdup.fasta
seqkit grep -s -r -i -p "^[ATCGatcg]+$" source/gisaid_h3n2_sequences.rmdup.fasta > source/gisaid_h3n2_sequences.rmdupn.noambig.fasta

# ibv victoria (vic)
seqkit rmdup -n source/gisaid_vic_sequences.fasta > source/gisaid_vic_sequences.rmdup.fasta
seqkit grep -s -r -i -p "^[ATCGatcg]+$" source/gisaid_vic_sequences.rmdup.fasta > source/gisaid_vic_sequences.rmdupn.noambig.fasta

```

## Downselection of GISAID Data with fludb and augur

1. Uplaod entire database with H1N1 and H3N2 sequences from:
   1. GISAID 
   2. JHH (Mostafa lab)
2. Query complete genomes
3. Concatenate all genomes
4. Augur filter - representative sequences (include all macha isolates)
5. Proceed with build

### Query Unique Isolates 

Build a query to ask
1. How many unique sample_IDs with HA sequences
2. How many unique sample_IDs with HA and NA sequences
3. How many unique sample_IDs with complete genomes (8 segment sequences)

```{python}
#| eval: false
import sqlite3

# Connect to the SQLite database
conn = sqlite3.connect('../fludb.db')  # Replace with your database path
cursor = conn.cursor()

# Query 1: Unique sample_IDs with HA sequences
query_ha = """
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sample_ID) 
    FROM influenza_genomes
    WHERE ha IS NOT NULL;
"""
ha_count = cursor.execute(query_ha).fetchone()[0]
print(f"Unique sample_IDs with HA sequences: {ha_count}")

# Query 2: Unique sample_IDs with HA and NA sequences
query_ha_na = """
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sample_ID)
    FROM influenza_genomes
    WHERE ha IS NOT NULL AND na IS NOT NULL;
"""
ha_na_count = cursor.execute(query_ha_na).fetchone()[0]
print(f"Unique sample_IDs with HA and NA sequences: {ha_na_count}")

# Query 3: Unique sample_IDs with complete genomes (8 segment sequences)
query_complete_genome = """
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sample_ID)
    FROM influenza_genomes
    WHERE pb2 IS NOT NULL AND pb1 IS NOT NULL AND pa IS NOT NULL
          AND ha IS NOT NULL AND np IS NOT NULL AND na IS NOT NULL
          AND mp IS NOT NULL AND ns IS NOT NULL;
"""
complete_genome_count = cursor.execute(query_complete_genome).fetchone()[0]
print(f"Unique sample_IDs with complete genomes: {complete_genome_count}")

# Close the connection
conn.close()
```

# Data Filtering augur filter - proceed with complete genomes only 
## Expand the `location` column in HA metadata to house continent and country in 2 seperate columns. Ignore levels 3 and 4 in location column as most rows do not have this information.

TODO: can we rewrite this with csvtk to be more streamlined? 

Function to extract region, country, and division from 

```{python}
import pandas as pd

def split_location(df, location_col="location", sequence_id_col="sequence_ID", sample_id_col="sample_ID"):
    """
    Enhances a metadata dataframe by splitting the location column and creating a strain column.

    Parameters:
        df (pd.DataFrame): Input DataFrame.
        location_col (str): Name of the column to split by " / ".
        sequence_id_col (str): Name of the sequence ID column.
        sample_id_col (str): Name of the sample ID column.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Enhanced DataFrame with added region, country, division, location_detailed, and strain columns.
    """

    def extract_levels(row, level):
        if isinstance(row, str):
            parts = row.split(" / ")
            return parts[level] if len(parts) > level else None
        return None

    # Apply location splitting
    df["region"] = df[location_col].apply(lambda x: extract_levels(x, 0))
    df["country"] = df[location_col].apply(lambda x: extract_levels(x, 1))
    df["division"] = df[location_col].apply(lambda x: extract_levels(x, 2))
    df["location_detailed"] = df[location_col].apply(lambda x: extract_levels(x, 3))

    # Create strain column
    df["strain"] = df[sequence_id_col].astype(str) + "_" + df[sample_id_col].astype(str)


    return df

h1n1_locations = pd.read_csv("../data/h1n1/genome/metadata.tsv", delimiter="\t")
h3n2_locations = pd.read_csv("../data/h3n2/genome/metadata.tsv", delimiter="\t")
vic_locations = pd.read_csv("../data/vic/genome/metadata.tsv", delimiter="\t")

h1n1_locations = split_location(h1n1_locations)
h3n2_locations = split_location(h3n2_locations) 
vic_locations = split_location(vic_locations) 

h1n1_locations.to_csv("../results/h1n1/genome/metadata.tsv", sep = "\t", index = False)
h3n2_locations.to_csv("../results/h3n2/genome/metadata.tsv", sep = "\t", index = False)
vic_locations.to_csv("../results/vic/genome/metadata.tsv", sep = "\t", index = False)

```


## Augur filter Downselection 

### h1n1 

#### filter only jhh isolates
 ```{shell}
 #| eval: false
augur filter \
    --metadata results/h1n1/genome/metadata.tsv\
    --sequences data/h1n1/genome/sequences.fasta \
    --min-length 13000 \
    --metadata-id-columns "sequence_ID" \
    --query "(location == 'JHH')" \
    --output-metadata results/h1n1/genome/jhh_filtered.tsv \
    --output-sequences results/h1n1/genome/jhh_filtered.fasta
 ```

#### filter and down-selected gisaid isolates

```{shell}
#| eval: false
augur filter \
    --metadata results/h1n1/genome/metadata.tsv\
    --sequences data/h1n1/genome/sequences.fasta \
    --min-length 13000 \
    --metadata-id-columns "sequence_ID" \
    --exclude-where "location=JHH" \
    --group-by week country \
    --subsample-max-sequences 2000 \
    --subsample-seed 180 \
    --output-metadata results/h1n1/genome/gisaid_filtered.tsv \
    --output-sequences results/h1n1/genome/gisaid_filtered.fasta
```

#### join filtered gisaid and jhh FASTA and metadata

join filtered metadata
```{shell}
#| eval: false
csvtk -t concat \
    results/h1n1/genome/gisaid_filtered.tsv \
    results/h1n1/genome/jhh_filtered.tsv \
    > results/h1n1/genome/filtered.tsv
```

join filtered fasta

```{shell}
    results/h1n1/genome/gisaid_filtered.fasta \
```

```{shell}
# vic

    results/vic/genome/filtered.tsv \

```


# Align concatenated Genomes 

TODO: The cattle H5N1 build aligns each segment individually and then prceeds with concatenating each alignment...consider this moving forward given that confidence intervals are still needed to calculate TMRCA for each identified mutation per segment.

```{shell}
#| eval: false

# h1n1 
augur align \
    --sequences results/h1n1/genome/filtered.fasta \
    --output results/h1n1/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --reference-sequence config/h1n1/genome.gb \
    --fill-gaps \
    --remove-reference \
    --nthreads 80

# h3n2 
augur align \
    --sequences results/h3n2/genome/filtered.fasta \
    --output results/h3n2/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --reference-sequence config/h3n2/genome.gb \
    --fill-gaps \
    --remove-reference \
    --nthreads 80

# vic
augur align \
    --sequences results/vic/genome/filtered.fasta \
    --output results/vic/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --reference-sequence config/vic/genome.gb \
    --fill-gaps \
    --remove-reference \
    --nthreads 200
```

# Build Raw Trees
```{shell}
#| eval: false

# h1n1 
augur tree \
    --nthreads 64 \
    --alignment results/h1n1/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --output results/h1n1/genome/tree_raw.nwk

# h3n2
augur tree \
    --nthreads 64 \
    --alignment results/h3n2/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --output results/h3n2/genome/tree_raw.nwk

# vic
augur tree \
    --nthreads 100 \
    --alignment results/vic/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --output results/vic/genome/tree_raw.nwk
```

# Refine raw tree 

Be sure to use `--stochastic-resolve` 

```{shell}
#| eval: false
# h1n1
augur refine \
    --tree results/h1n1/genome/tree_raw.nwk \
    --alignment results/h1n1/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --metadata results/h1n1/genome/filtered_clades.tsv \
    --metadata-id-columns "sequence_ID" \
    --output-tree results/h1n1/genome/tree.nwk \
    --output-node-data results/h1n1/genome/branch_lengths.json \
    --timetree \
    --date-confidence \
    --clock-std-dev 0.00211 \
    --stochastic-resolve \
    --coalescent "opt" \
    --date-inference "marginal"

# h3n2 
augur refine \
    --tree results/h3n2/genome/tree_raw.nwk \
    --alignment results/h3n2/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --metadata results/h3n2/genome/filtered_clades.tsv \
    --metadata-id-columns "sequence_ID" \
    --output-tree results/h3n2/genome/tree.nwk \
    --output-node-data results/h3n2/genome/branch_lengths.json \
    --timetree \
    --date-confidence \
    --clock-std-dev 0.00211 \
    --stochastic-resolve \
    --coalescent "opt" \
    --date-inference "marginal"

# vic 
augur refine \
    --tree results/vic/genome/tree_raw.nwk \
    --alignment results/vic/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --metadata results/vic/genome/filtered_clades.tsv \
    --metadata-id-columns "sequence_ID" \
    --output-tree results/vic/genome/tree.nwk \
    --output-node-data results/vic/genome/branch_lengths.json \
    --timetree \
    --date-confidence \
    --clock-std-dev 0.00211 \
    --stochastic-resolve \
    --coalescent "opt" \
    --verbosity 6 /
    --date-inference "marginal"
```

## Defining the genomic evolutionary rate

What is the most appropriate way to calculate the clock rate for the entire genome? Louise Moncla's build calculates the average of the segments weighted by each of their lengths as defined [here](https://github.com/nextstrain/avian-flu/blob/387e6427d80c6d72559505a0d7362af24b97dca9/Snakefile#L183). The standard deviation here is calculated using the `--clock-std-dev` flag and has been set to 0.002 in the seasonal-flu builds and 0.00211 in the H5N1 cattle builds. 

>        --clock-rate {define} \
>        --clock-std-dev = 0.002 \ #defined by other builds

```{shell}
    --tree results/vic/genome/tree.nwk \
    --alignment results/vic/genome/aligned.fasta \
    --output-node-data results/vic/genome/nt_muts.json \
    --inference "joint"
```

# Augur Frequencies

Frequencies is must be exported as ${name}_tip-frequencies.json with the name being the exported name build  https://docs.nextstrain.org/en/latest/reference/data-formats.html
Be sure that the name matches the build output name as listed above! 

Make sure this is exported to the auspice folder for proper export

```{shell}

# h1n1 
augur frequencies \
    --method kde \
    --tree results/h1n1/genome/tree.nwk \
    --narrow-bandwidth 0.25 \
    --wide-bandwidth 0.083 \
    --proportion-wide 0.02 \
    --pivot-interval 1 \
    --include-internal-nodes \
    --metadata results/h1n1/genome/filtered_clades.tsv \
    --output auspice/h1n1/genome_tip-frequencies.json 

# h3n2

augur frequencies \
    --method kde \
    --tree results/h3n2/genome/tree.nwk \
    --narrow-bandwidth 0.25 \
    --wide-bandwidth 0.083 \
    --proportion-wide 0.02 \
    --pivot-interval 1 \
    --include-internal-nodes \
    --metadata results/h3n2/genome/filtered_clades.tsv \
    --output auspice/h3n2/genome_tip-frequencies.json 

# vic

augur frequencies \
    --method kde \
    --tree results/vic/genome/tree.nwk \
    --include-internal-nodes \
    --metadata results/vic/genome/filtered_clades.tsv \
    --output auspice/vic/genome_tip-frequencies.json 
```
